issues.body:
The record specifies `SUM` as "count and numeric sum" and `AVG` as "count and numeric sum and derives the result", with a differential test oracle asserting equivalence to full evaluation. sparq's actual SUM (crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs:9881 `sum_values`) is an order-dependent left fold starting at `Num::Int(0)` and promoting through `Num::binop`, then canonicalised via `num_canonical_term`. Two consequences make a single running accumulator wrong:

- Type provenance. Group {"1"^^xsd:integer, "2.5E0"^^xsd:double} folds to a double. Delete the double and re-evaluation yields "1"^^xsd:integer, while an incrementally maintained accumulator yields "1.0E0"^^xsd:double. These are distinct RDF terms, so the canonical group binding — and therefore the emitted add/remove pair — diverges from re-evaluation. A subtraction cannot restore the pre-promotion type.
- Ordered f64 arithmetic. For xsd:double groups, add-then-subtract does not reproduce the fold order, so the maintained value can differ from the recomputed value in the low bits. Integer overflow behaviour also differs: `binop` returning `None` yields `Value::Error` on one path but may be avoided by the incremental path (or vice versa).

The record also does not say how a group whose SUM is poisoned to `Value::Error` by a non-numeric contributor (the `as_numeric` failure path) is maintained across deletion of that contributor.
issues.fix_hint: Make the aggregate state type-aware rather than a single accumulator: maintain per-numeric-class counted sub-sums (integer, decimal, float, double) plus a count of non-numeric/errored contributors, and derive the group binding by re-folding those buckets in the engine's promotion order so the result type is a function of the current membership, not of history. Declare xsd:double SUM/AVG either ineligible for IVM or explicitly recompute-on-touch for any group containing a double, and state that rule in the eligibility section. Add a `state a group's aggregate is recomputed from scratch when the errored-contributor count transitions to zero` rule. Extend the verification corpus with: mixed integer/decimal/double groups where the promoting member is deleted, non-numeric contributor insert/delete, and integer-overflow boundaries.
issues.title: Incremental SUM/AVG state loses numeric type provenance and cannot reproduce sum_values' ordered fold

issues.body:
The record specifies "`MIN` and `MAX` store a counted ordered multiset of values", implying one fixed ordering. crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs:9895 `minmax_values` switches regime based on group membership: if every member is numeric it compares by numeric value (`num_compare`) and returns `num_canonical_term(best)`; if any member is non-numeric it falls back to the lenient total-order `compare_values` over terms. Those two orders disagree (numeric value equality vs term ordering across types), and the returned term differs in canonicalisation.

So a multiset ordered under one regime yields the wrong extremum the moment the last non-numeric member is deleted (regime flips numeric-only) or the first non-numeric member is inserted (regime flips to term order). This is the classic value-equality-vs-term-identity trap: distinct lexical forms that are numerically equal (e.g. "1"^^xsd:integer vs "1.0"^^xsd:decimal vs whitespace-padded lexicals) collapse under one order and not the other, so a multiset keyed on term identity can pick a different representative term than re-evaluation does. There is also a third fold (the temporals fast path noted at exec.rs:9920) the record does not mention.
issues.fix_hint: Specify the extremum state as: a counted multiset keyed by TERM identity, plus a counter of non-numeric members (and of temporal members if that fold is in scope). Derive MIN/MAX by running the engine's own `minmax_values` over the current distinct members rather than by reading the head of a pre-sorted structure, or maintain one ordered index per regime and select by the non-numeric counter. Either way, state explicitly that the representative TERM (not just the value) must equal what full evaluation returns. Add corpus cases: numerically-equal-but-lexically-distinct extrema, deletion of the last non-numeric member, repeated extrema with counts > 1, and mixed temporal/numeric groups.
issues.title: MIN/MAX "counted ordered multiset" cannot express the engine's two comparison regimes

issues.body:
The per-commit algorithm ("Verify that `C` is the immediate successor of `last_cdc_sequence`"), the bootstrap ("Read the durable CDC tail cursor", "Re-read the CDC tail. Replay every later record"), lag recovery ("replays missing records from the segmented log"), and history storage ("a separate segmented log rooted below the configured change-stream directory") all require a live `ChangeLog`. Per crates/sparq-server/src/streams.rs:59-63 the change stream is a DOUBLE opt-in — the `change-stream` cargo feature AND a configured log directory (`--change-stream <DIR>` / `SPARQ_CHANGE_STREAM`) — and is OFF by default; the route 404s otherwise.

The record notes this conditionally once under "Existing seams" but then treats CDC as unconditionally present, never states that `subscription-ivm` requires it, and the "Failure and recovery rules" table has no row for it. As written, a reader implementing this would ship a feature that cannot bootstrap or verify commit contiguity in a default deployment, and the history root would be unconfigured.
issues.fix_hint: State the dependency explicitly: `subscription-ivm` requires the `change-stream` feature AND a configured change-stream directory; either make the cargo feature depend on it, or add a documented degraded mode. Add a row to the failure/recovery table: "change-stream disabled or unconfigured at registration -> subscribe in `reevaluate` mode" (and note that v2 `subscribed` then reports `mode: "reevaluate"` with no `historyCursor`). Also state where the answer-history log lives when the change-stream directory is configured but the operator wants history disabled independently.
issues.title: Undeclared hard dependency on the change-stream double opt-in, which is OFF by default

issues.body:
crates/sparq-server/src/subscriptions.rs:44-46 documents a known v1 limitation: "the engine relabels blank nodes between evaluations, so a result row containing a blank node can show up as a remove+add pair across commits even when it is semantically unchanged." The diff's row identity is the serialised canonical binding object (subscriptions.rs:22-26), so the label is load-bearing.

IVM builds leaf relations directly from stored quads, so its labels are whatever the store carries and are stable across commits. That is a BEHAVIOUR CHANGE relative to re-evaluation, and it breaks the record's central acceptance criterion — "differential tests that run the same eligible query through IVM and through full evaluation after every commit, comparing counted internal results and emitted set deltas". For any query whose results can bind a blank node, the two paths will disagree by construction (spurious remove+add on the re-evaluation side), making the oracle either flaky or wrong. The eligibility fragment says nothing about blank nodes in patterns or in projected results, and the verification corpus does not list them.
issues.fix_hint: Decide and write down one of: (a) blank-node-producing projections are INELIGIBLE for IVM (fail-closed, consistent with the rest of the classifier) — the classifier can decide this statically from the projected variables and pattern positions only if bnode-binding is statically knowable, otherwise fall back at bootstrap when the initial snapshot contains a bnode; or (b) IVM defines stable bnode labels and the design states that v2 `ivm` mode intentionally FIXES the v1 relabeling limitation, in which case the differential oracle must compare modulo bnode isomorphism rather than by canonical string key, and that must be spelled out. Add "results containing blank nodes" to the verification corpus either way.
issues.title: Blank nodes unaddressed: eligibility does not exclude them and the differential oracle will diverge

issues.body:
Step 3 states the two-relation rule correctly: `d(R join S) = (dR join Sold) + (Rold join dS) + (dR join dS)`. It then generalises with "For a longer BGP, the same rule is applied in the plan's fixed left-deep order, with each stage reading a consistent old-plus-current-commit view."

For the identity to hold at stage n, the delta must be joined against the OLD (pre-commit) intermediate relation, with the delta-delta term added exactly once. "old-plus-current-commit view" reads as joining against a relation that already has this commit's delta applied, which is precisely the double-counting error (the dR join dS term is then counted twice). Because the record is the spec an implementer will follow, this ambiguity is the kind that produces a silent multiplicity error under bag/counted semantics rather than a crash — and support counts are the only thing standing between that and a wrong wire delta.
issues.fix_hint: Replace the sentence with an explicit recurrence, e.g. for left-deep stages P_1..P_k define d(P_1..P_i) = (d(P_1..P_{i-1}) join Leaf_i^old) + (P_1..P_{i-1}^old join dLeaf_i) + (d(P_1..P_{i-1}) join dLeaf_i), and state that every `^old` operand is the pre-commit relation and that stage state is only advanced after the whole commit's deltas are computed (matching step 7's publish-after-durable-append). Add a corpus case that changes two or more leaves in a single commit AND has a leaf appearing in more than one join stage, asserting counted-relation equality against full evaluation.
issues.title: Multi-way delta-join wording ("old-plus-current-commit view") admits a double-counting reading

issues.body:
The history record persists `added_results` and `removed_results` — i.e. actual query answers — to a segmented log with configurable retention. Two gaps:

- Authorization. The record says history "uses the same read authentication gate as subscription registration" and that "Deployments needing per-principal isolation must place the server behind an authorization layer". But sparq ships an in-server per-principal authorization surface (crates/sparq-server/src/solid_authz.rs, plus the WAC/ACP/ODRL work), so advising an external layer understates what is available. As specified, any principal holding the single `--auth-token-read` token (crates/sparq-server/src/subscriptions.rs:138-150) who obtains a `subscription_key` can read another principal's answer history.
- Erasure. Answers survive deletion of the underlying quads for the whole retention window, which cuts against the crypto-erase-at-rest direction in research/crypto-erase-at-rest.md and against any right-to-erasure posture. The only stated protection is "the persisted record never contains bearer credentials".

Neither is fatal to the design, but both should be decided in the record rather than deferred to the implementer.
issues.fix_hint: Bind the subscription_key to the authenticated principal at registration and require that principal on history retrieval (not just the read gate), so the key is a lookup handle rather than a capability; where solid_authz is active, state that history retrieval is subject to the same per-resource checks the original subscription passed. Add an explicit erasure rule: history segments participate in the same at-rest key/erase scheme as the change stream, retention has a documented default upper bound, and there is a way to purge a subscription's history on unsubscribe. Add a security note that history is a durable plaintext copy of answers, and add a corpus case asserting that a second principal cannot retrieve a first principal's history.
issues.title: Durable answer history is a new at-rest copy of query answers with only the coarse read gate and no erasure story

verdict.summary: Docs-only design record for standing-query IVM. Its account of the existing seams is accurate and verifiable against the tree (subscriptions.rs re-evaluate+diff over a coalescing tokio watch channel with documented set-semantics divergence; sparq-serve ChangeRecord/ChangeLog with REBASE gap markers; streams.rs change-stream double opt-in); it honestly answers open question 6 of research/competitive-feature-analysis-2026-07.md and disclaims that no implementation has landed. The v1/v2 negotiation, counted-multiset zero-crossing rule, fail-closed eligibility classifier, and durable-append-before-cursor-advance ordering are sound. But as written the record admits several concrete divergences from full evaluation, so it is not yet a safe spec to implement against. (1) Incremental SUM/AVG state ("count and numeric sum") cannot reproduce sparq's aggregate: exec.rs sum_values is an order-dependent left fold over Num from Int(0) with type promotion, so deleting the only xsd:double contributor leaves an accumulator typed double where re-evaluation yields integer/decimal; f64 subtraction is also non-associative. (2) MIN/MAX in exec.rs minmax_values has two regimes (all-numeric value comparison returning a canonicalised numeric term vs lenient total-order term comparison when any member is non-numeric); one counted ordered multiset silently returns the wrong term when the last non-numeric member is deleted. (3) The per-commit algorithm, bootstrap and history root depend unconditionally on durable CDC, but change-stream is a double opt-in that is OFF by default and the record never states the dependency nor lists it in the fallback table. (4) Blank nodes are unaddressed even though subscriptions.rs documents engine bnode relabeling as a known limitation; the differential oracle will diverge and eligibility does not exclude bnode-producing results. Also see the multi-way join-order wording and the answer-history retention/authz gaps below.
